To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isostable distribution is a key feature of the energy-optimal stimulus, that the energy-optimal method is robust to noise and that the energy-optimality of the method is maintained in a realistic model of the myocardium.

we developed an energy-optimal methodology for synchronization of the cells of an excitatory medium, which is illustrated for a myocardium-based model, and the optimal stimulus takes the system to a target set, where the isostable are diffuse, thereby achieving synchronization of the system.
we have developed a novel energy-optimality based method to synchronize the cells of an oscillatory medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of optimal defibrillation strategies which can be implemented using a minimal amount of energy.
the design of energy-optimal methods for synchronization of excitable media.
the study of the synchronization properties of excitable media and with the development of energy-efficient defibrillation strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed energy-optimal method is a significant step towards the development of energy optimal strategies for the defibrillation of cardiac arrhythmias.
the energy-optimal methodology proposed in this paper is a novel approach for synchronization of the cells within an excitatory medium during spiral wave propagation.
the proposed methodology is a promising tool to study and control excitable media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a methodology that is based on the isostable concept, and we applied the methodology for the synchronization of excitable media.
the energy-optimal methodology can be used as a tool for the design of energy-efficient cardiac defibrillators.
the optimal defibrillation protocol for an excitable medium is the one which minimizes the total energy required for synchronization of the medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isostables are a powerful tool to characterize the dynamics and to develop optimal control methods for synchronization of excitable media.
the energy-optimal stimulus can be computed by solving a nonlinear optimization problem with a convex objective function and convex constraints.
a stimulus can be found that takes an excitable medium into a state where the dynamics are slow and the cells are synchronized.
